_purpose: Canonical 3D-scene vantages for the visual-regression + perf sweeps (scripts/probe-sweep.js). This is the golden spec: each vantage teleports the probe to a fixed camera + time/sea, captures one screenshot, and records fps. The `expect` text is what a correct frame looks like; `regressions` lists the specific failures this vantage exists to catch (each has bitten a real release). Data-driven per the infinite-of-x rule - add a vantage here, both sweeps pick it up. Coordinates are the same debug/camera_request.json + debug/showcase_request.json fields lib.rs polls.
_perf_note: perf_floor_fps is an advisory lower bound at this vantage on the dev machine (RTX 4070). The perf sweep flags a stop below it; it is a smoke threshold, not a hard gate.
_clock_note: READ THIS BEFORE PICKING A `time`. The showcase `time` field is a GLOBAL clock, not the local solar hour at the vantage (src/engine/ipc.rs:200-205 feeds it straight into the world clock). The local solar hour is roughly `time + lon/15`. So time 12.0 is local noon only near lon 0; at lon 138.8 (the Fuji vantages) time 12.0 is about 21:15 LOCAL and the frame comes back as a night scene. Pick `time = desired_local_hour - lon/15`, wrapped into 0..24. This trap cost `ground-storm-inslab` its whole purpose from v0.1070 to v0.1073: it was installed as the permanent BUG-049 daylight gate and was silently rendering at night, so every cloud LIGHTING change was being judged in the dark.

vantages.desc: Ground level in the Sahara at local noon, facing the horizon
vantages.expect: A deep, saturated blue sky dome fading to a pale warm band at the horizon, over rolling tan sand. Bright and clearly daytime.
regressions: NO stars visible (v0.913-era daytime star bleed)
no washed-out near-white dome (v0.918 exposure)
no hard-edged black shell or ring around the horizon

vantages.desc: 8 m above a calm sea, grazing angle to the horizon
vantages.expect: Deep rippled blue water reading as gentle rolling swell all the way to a clean horizon, under a blue-to-warm sky. Fine surface structure, not glassy-flat.
regressions: NO black/white zebra banding (v0.921 analytic-wave aliasing)
no concentric moire interference rings
no white-out sheet at the grazing angle
no cloud-deck sheet band riding the horizon line (v0.958 low-camera aerial fade; clouds-off A/B 2026-07-25)

vantages.desc: 6 m above a storm sea, grazing angle
vantages.expect: Dark blue-grey choppy water with organic white foam streaks riding the wave crests (roughly a third coverage at most). Reads as a rough sea, not a white sheet. SKY: the deck overhead is a few LARGE masses with a defined base that dissolves into the horizon haze band, not a distant field of small uniform puffs (reworded v0.1074, when the High path started marching the slab at its designed 25.5-76.5 km instead of 76-128 km). NOTE: this vantage pins `sea` but NOT `weather`, so the live condition drifts - it captured as Clear at v0.1074. Judge the SEA STATE here, which `sea` does pin; use ground-storm-inslab for storm lighting.
regressions: no full-white ocean (v0.906 whiteout)
foam on crests only, not flat areas
no zebra banding even in chop
no cloud-deck sheet band riding the horizon line (v0.958 low-camera aerial fade; clouds-off A/B 2026-07-25)

vantages.desc: Open ocean from a 30 m eye - the water-shell COVERAGE case.
vantages.expect: Wave field carries to the horizon. NO flat pale plates: those are the coarse backstop shell showing through where the wave shell ran out of leaves. A high eye sees far more sea than a 3 m eye, so this is where the water leaf budget is actually tested (v0.1048: the operator hit it at 13 m with terrain_split_px = 2). SKY: the cloud deck reads as a few LARGE near masses with a defined, continuous base, subtending tens of degrees. (Reworded v0.1074: the old text was written against a deck the High path was marching at 76-128 km, three times its designed distance, where it read as a remote field of small same-sized puffs under a scalloped edge. The slab now marches at 25.5-76.5 km, so the same weather draws far fewer, far bigger elements.)
regressions: water-shell coverage / backstop show-through
cross-LOD seams at distance

no remote painted ceiling of many small same-sized puffs - if the deck's elements are small and uniform again, cloud_layer_volumetric has stopped consuming material.params.w and is marching a slab thickness too high (the v0.1025-v0.1073 dead write, fixed v0.1074)

vantages.desc: Ground level near Mt Fuji in a conifer forest, morning
vantages._settle_note: 75 s, NOT the 25 s this carried through v0.1078. MEASURED 2026-07-31: at 25 s this vantage captures 43-48 ms while the scene is still streaming, and it keeps getting heavier for another ~40 s before it settles at 93.7 ms +/- 5.8 (10.7 fps) on the operator's max-quality rig config. So the sweep was reporting 21.3 and 18.8 fps and passing an 18 fps floor at 55% of the real number. Every perf figure taken here before v0.1079 is measuring a half-built forest. probe-sweep.js `settle_s` is a plain sleep (scripts/probe-sweep.js:236) with no steady-state detection; a proper fix waits for [PatchBatch] to stop changing in run.log, which is a rig change, not a data change.
vantages.expect: Dense green ground with real 3D conifer trees standing around the camera - visible brown trunks, needled canopies - and BAKED SILHOUETTE cards, ragged crown outlines with sky visible through their edges, never plain rectangles, carrying the forest toward the horizon. Grass underfoot.
regressions: 3D tree MODELS present, not just flat cards (v0.923 default-off regression)
no bare ground where a forest should be (bare-forest card-hide bug)
trunks visible, not floating canopies

NO flat rectangular slabs anywhere in the tree field: every card past the 3D-model ring shows a crown outline with sky visible through its edge. 6 of the 8 rows in data/vegetation/trees.ron are procedural (model: "") and had NO atlas tile, so they fell through planet_chunks.rs:1925 to plain coloured trunk+canopy rectangles; fir and pine took the sprite path but a SHIPPED build has no assets/models/ (.github/workflows/build-desktop.yml copies data/ + assets/icons/ + assets/shaders/ only), so the bake aborted, tree_atlas_ready stayed false and their cards painted the flat green fallback at 90-fragment-main.wgsl:824. Photographed as a picket fence of grey slabs at v0.1078.

NO storm-strength lean in calm weather: the same wind uniform (light7_cone_inner, wind_dir_world.xyz + speed m/s) must produce a near-upright stand here. Crowns sway but stay centred over their bases.

vantages.desc: 150 m above a forested Fuji slope, looking down across the canopy. The CARD rung seen from above, which is where the operator's "black squares in a grid" verdict came from. Added 2026-07-31: there were 25 vantages and exactly one forest one, and both forest vantages sat at 30 m INSIDE the stand, so the 70 m-to-cutoff card stage - the largest-screen-area vegetation LOD at any elevated view - had no clean rig coverage at all.
vantages.expect: A forested slope filling the lower two-thirds of the frame, seen from above the canopy: individual crowns readable as separate ragged silhouettes with a clear sunlit-top / shaded-flank split, the canopy mass reading DARKER than the open ground beyond it. (look_offset_deg is measured from straight down, so 72 aims about 18 degrees below the horizon. showcase `time` is a GLOBAL clock; local solar hour = time + lon/15, so lon 138.8 needs time 2.9 for local noon - see _clock_note.)
regressions: NO flat rectangular slabs in the canopy band - the finding-1 gate, at the distance where it is most visible

the forest band's mean luminance must be BELOW that of the adjacent open ground (real canopy albedo 0.08-0.15 vs grass 0.20-0.25). Card shading normals were pinned to the radial up at planet_chunks.rs:1686 and :1727 (the v0.896 black-slab fix), so cards lit exactly like the terrain and a distant forest read as a flat green carpet painted on the hillside
per-tree luminance variance in the canopy band must exceed 8/255 - a uniform flat mass means the cards still have no directional shading

NO black slabs either: the v0.896 failure this replaced. A card normal blended toward the card facing must never reach N.L = 0 under an overhead sun, and a two-sided card must not go dark on its back face

vantages.desc: 400 km over the Sahara, the atmosphere limb in frame against stars
vantages.expect: The curved planet surface below a THIN bright blue atmosphere limb that fades smoothly into a black star-filled sky. Stars visible right down to the edge of the atmosphere band.
regressions: NO hard-edged opaque black shell/ring around the planet (v0.925 orbital occlusion bug)
the limb fades to stars, it does not cut off

no straight white cloud slivers hovering ABOVE the atmosphere limb against black sky, and no deck jump between a 390 km and a 420 km capture (the drawn-shell ratio flips at ~399 km; before the v0.1074 slab fix the High path ignored that ratio, so the deck sat at 76-128 km below the flip and snapped back into the atmosphere above it)

vantages.desc: Level flight at 40 km looking at the horizon - the camera is INSIDE the cloud slab. The altitude that proves the deck is where the constants say it is; it was the ladder step that exposed the v0.1025-v0.1073 dead write.
vantages.expect: At 40 km the camera is INSIDE the cloud layer: cloud masses pass AT eye level, with the blue atmosphere limb and the ocean visible past them. Nothing renders BELOW eye level by construction: below-horizon rays get no cloud-shell fragment (the shell backface is depth-rejected behind the ocean), so judge the at-and-above band only (critic-measured v0.1074: the change stops dead at the eye-level row). No cloud sits above the black-sky boundary.
regressions: NO cloud ceiling hanging above the camera at 40 km with the atmosphere limb, stars and ocean all BELOW it (v0.1025-v0.1073 dead-write: cloud_layer_volumetric never consumed material.params.w, so the slab marched at 76-128 km instead of 25.5-76.5 km at every altitude under ~400 km)
no flat white sheet with a straight horizontal top edge (the drawn-shell crossing artifact, visible at 110 km before the fix)

vantages.desc: Ground under an active storm at LOCAL noon, camera inside/under the low deck. The weather + in-slab combination clear-sky vantages never exercise. Runs on the HIGH cloud tier: scripts/probe-sweep.js never sets a cloud quality and src/config.rs:739 defaults to "high", so this vantage exercises High, NOT Medium. MEDIUM HAS ZERO RIG COVERAGE - no vantage anywhere in this file selects it - which is why any change to the Medium path is unverifiable here and must not be made without adding its own storm + in-slab coverage first.
vantages.expect: A dark stormy sky with a low ragged deck overhead at LOCAL NOON. Rain-dimmed but clearly DAYLIT: terrain and horizon readable, ground colours identifiable. The scene stays recognizable as weather, not abstract shapes. (showcase `time` is a GLOBAL clock; local solar hour = time + lon/15, so lon 138.8 needs time 2.9 for local noon - see _clock_note.)
regressions: NO screen-filling concentric rings or banded shells (v0.1069.0 clouds slab-bounds regression: storm lowered the deck, in-slab camera flipped shell_ratio, Medium path consumed params.w bounds for the first time and the march ran on collapsed bounds; caught live by the operator, reverted v0.1070.0)
no giant lattice/mesh silhouette filling the view
no inverted sky (stars below the horizon at ground level)
NO stars or Milky Way visible through the sky at any hour - an overcast storm deck is optically opaque (observed at v0.1073)
whole-frame mean luminance must be above 60 (22.0 at v0.1073, because global clock 12.0 at lon 138.8 was local ~21:00 and this gate was silently a NIGHT scene)

NO flat rectangular slabs anywhere in the tree field - the mid-field vegetation is clearest here of any vantage (photographed at v0.1078: a row of pale grey vertical slabs with hard straight tops and hard vertical sides, repeating across the frame). Every card past the 3D-model ring must show a crown outline with sky through its edge

Under 12-25 m/s storm wind the whole stand LEANS DOWNWIND: every crown visibly displaced from over its base, and every tree in frame leaning the SAME compass direction, displacement growing with tree height. NO upright calm-day forest under a storm, and NO fanning (no two crowns leaning in opposite directions). Before v0.1079 the foliage wind was a hardcoded OBJECT-space vector at 00-bindings-vertex.wgsl:594 with a zero-mean sway and no WeatherState wind-speed input, and each instance's random yaw (planet_chunks.rs:1883) rotated it, so trees swayed in random directions at one fixed calm-day amplitude

vantages.desc: Heavy snow on the EXPERIMENTAL GPU particle path (gpu_precip flip). The stride-mismatch class only manifests here, never on the default CPU path.
vantages.expect: Ordinary falling snow: small white flakes over the forest scene, ground and trees clearly visible. Identical in character to the CPU-path snow.
regressions: NO giant colored spheres, blobs or streaks (BUG-050: the sim shader wrote 64-byte vec3-aligned records into the 52-byte packed vertex stream, so every instance after the first read shifted garbage; sizes picked up world coordinates, colors picked up neighbouring floats)
flakes must be small and white, not cyan/magenta ellipses

vantages.desc: Earth from orbit with an active Snow condition: precipitation must NOT follow the camera into space. This class has recurred twice (v0.1064 low flight; 2026-07-31 the None-altitude hole from FTL).
vantages.expect: The blue marble in clean black space. Weather HUD says Snow, but ZERO flakes anywhere in frame: precipitation lives under the cloud deck.
regressions: NO white flakes over the planet or the starfield (snow-in-space: surface_altitude_m None was defaulted to 0 m, so the tropopause gate passed in orbit)
